fine_lines.title: house vs home
fine_lines.explanation_ar: house هو المبنى نفسه: الجدران والسقف، شيء مادي تستطيع لمسه. home هو المكان الذي تعيش فيه وتشعر فيه بالأمان والانتماء، فهو شعور وليس مجرد مبنى. ليس كل house يصبح home إلا إذا شعرت فيه بالراحة والانتماء.

examples.sentence: They bought a big house with a garden.
After a long trip, it's nice to be home.
This new flat finally feels like home.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A "house" is the building itself: the walls and the roof, a physical thing you can touch. "Home" is the place where you live and feel safe and that you belong. It's a feeling, not just a building. A house only becomes a home when you feel comfortable there.

fine_lines.title: clean vs tidy
fine_lines.explanation_ar: clean تصف مستوى النظافة: لا يوجد أوساخ أو غبار. tidy تصف مستوى الترتيب: كل شيء في مكانه. قد تكون الغرفة نظيفة جداً لكنها غير مرتبة (أشياء مبعثرة)، وقد تكون مرتبة لكنها غير نظيفة.

examples.sentence: The floor is clean, but there are toys everywhere.

fine_lines.explanation_en: "Clean" is about dirt: there is no dirt or dust. "Tidy" is about order: everything is in its place. A room can be very clean but not tidy (things everywhere), or tidy but not clean.

fine_lines.title: attic vs basement
fine_lines.explanation_ar: attic هي المساحة في أعلى البيت تحت السقف مباشرة. basement عكسها: غرفة تحت الطابق الأرضي (القبو أو البدروم).

examples.sentence: We found old photos in the attic.
The basement is dark and cold.

fine_lines.explanation_en: The "attic" is the space at the top of a house, right under the roof. The "basement" is the opposite: a room below the ground floor.

expressions.meaning_ar: كل شيء يمكن تخيله / مبالغة في أخذ أو جمع أشياء كثيرة
expressions.example: It was a two-day trip, but he packed everything but the kitchen sink.
expressions.meaning_en: absolutely everything; taking or packing far too many things

expressions.example: Now I feel at home in this city.
expressions.meaning_en: to feel relaxed and comfortable, as if you were in your own home
to start living in a new home

expressions.meaning_ar: يدخل ماشياً / يقع في (فخ) / يصطدم بشيء
expressions.example: He wasn't looking and walked into the door.
expressions.meaning_en: to enter a place; to hit something by accident while walking; to fall into a trap

expressions.example: I still write everything by hand. Old habits die hard.
expressions.meaning_en: it's hard to stop doing things you have always done

expressions.meaning_ar: خيط رفيع: فرق بسيط بين شيئين متشابهين
expressions.example: There's a fine line between brave and crazy.
expressions.meaning_en: a very small difference between two similar things

grammar.title: Past perfect: the past of the past
grammar.explanation_ar: الماضي التام (had + التصريف الثالث) يشبه «الفلاش باك» في الأفلام. عندما نتكلم عن حدثين في الماضي، نضع الحدث الأقدم في الماضي التام، والحدث الذي جاء بعده في الماضي البسيط. كلمة already اختيارية وتعني «بالفعل».
examples: When I arrived at the airport, the plane had already taken off.
I couldn't pay the bill because I had left my wallet at home.
She passed the exam easily because she had studied hard.
grammar.explanation_en: The past perfect (had + past participle) is like a flashback in a film. When we talk about two events in the past, we use the past perfect for the earlier event and the past simple for the event that came after it. The word "already" is optional.

grammar.title: where and that for describing things
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم where بمعنى «حيث / المكان الذي» لوصف الأماكن، ونستخدم that أو which بمعنى «الذي» لوصف الأشياء.
examples: The kitchen is where you cook.
A bed is something that you lie on to sleep.
grammar.explanation_en: We use "where" to describe places (the place in which...), and "that" or "which" to describe things.

grammar.title: help + verb (no to)
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد الفعل help يمكن أن يأتي الفعل مباشرة بدون to: help (someone) carry. استخدام to بعدها صحيح أيضاً لكنه أقل في الكلام اليومي.
examples: He helped carry the heavy bookshelf.
Can you help me move the sofa?
grammar.explanation_en: After "help", you can put the verb directly, without "to": help (someone) carry. Using "to" is also correct, but it is less common in everyday speech.

questions.question: Where do you hang your clothes?
questions.explanation_en: A wardrobe is the cupboard where you keep your clothes.

questions.question: A room below the ground floor is called a:
questions.explanation_en: A basement is the room below the ground floor.

questions.question: After two years in London, the city finally feels like ___.
questions.explanation_ar: home تعبّر عن شعور الانتماء والراحة.
questions.explanation_en: "Home" expresses a feeling of belonging and comfort.

questions.question: The room has no dust, but things are everywhere. It is clean but not ___.
questions.explanation_en: "Tidy" means in order; "clean" means without dirt.

questions.question: When I got to the station, the train ___.
questions.explanation_ar: مغادرة القطار حدثت أولاً، فنستخدم الماضي التام.
questions.explanation_en: The train left first, so we use the past perfect.

questions.question: I couldn't open the door because I ___ my keys.
questions.explanation_ar: فقدان المفاتيح حدث قبل محاولة فتح الباب = had lost.
questions.explanation_en: Losing the keys happened before trying to open the door, so we say "had lost".

questions.question: "She packed everything but the kitchen sink" means she packed:
questions.explanation_ar: التعبير يعني أنها أخذت أشياء كثيرة جداً.
questions.explanation_en: The expression means she took far too many things.

questions.question: What do you use to dry yourself after a shower?
questions.explanation_en: A towel is what you use to dry yourself.

questions.question: The old stove was ___ — it was covered with dust.
